- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., >0.27) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) — model ignores downside risk, leading to lagged corrections.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +/–), model overfits short-term momentum, causing false peaks or troughs.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1st 5–10 days) when sentiment is bullish, then underestimates later correction.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate later half (e.g., days 15–30) when sentiment turns negative or stabilizes — model fails to adjust for tapering momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model should reduce forecast slope to avoid “over-optimism” bias.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.80 to -0.5), model should reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to reflect risk reversal.
